title: Sell Mineral Rights in Brookhaven, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Brookhaven, WV | Monongalia County
metaDescription: Brookhaven, WV near Morgantown sits over old farmland mineral tracts. We buy Monongalia County interests and heir shares directly, title-checked first.
heroLead: Brookhaven sits close enough to Morgantown that a lot of its land has been absorbed into the university city's growth, but the mineral rights underneath it still trace back to farm tracts leased long before the subdivisions arrived.
intro: Monongalia County's mix of university-driven residential growth and steady Marcellus leasing means Brookhaven's mineral ownership history looks a lot like Bridgeport's in Harrison County: surface developed for housing, minerals reserved and passed down separately, often to heirs who no longer live nearby.
We buy mineral and royalty interests around Brookhaven directly, tracing your specific tract back through the original farm parcel description rather than the current residential lot lines.

sections.heading: Suburban growth over a rural mineral estate
paragraphs: As Morgantown expanded, farmland near Brookhaven was subdivided for housing while mineral rights were frequently reserved separately in the sale. The result is a mineral estate whose boundaries no longer match any surface lot, which we confirm through the original deed description.

sections.heading: Monongalia County leasing activity
paragraphs: Monongalia County has seen ongoing Marcellus development, and a Brookhaven-area tract may sit within a modern pooled unit even if the family hasn't received a check in years or was never told the well went into production.

sections.heading: Confirming ownership before we make an offer
paragraphs: We pull the recorded severance deed and any subsequent probate or transfer records to confirm exactly who holds the mineral interest today, then check current lease and unit status before naming a number.

This step matters more near Brookhaven than in a rural farming community, because a subdivided tract can produce confusion between the surface owner and the mineral owner, and title companies handling a home sale rarely flag a mineral reservation buried in a decades-old deed.

faqs.question: My family's old farm near Brookhaven is now a subdivision. Do we still own the minerals?
faqs.answer: If the mineral rights were reserved when the land was sold for development, yes. We verify the reservation deed as part of our review.

faqs.question: How do I know if there's an active well or unit on my tract?
faqs.answer: We check the current lease and unit records for Monongalia County covering your specific tract description.

faqs.question: Can you buy my interest even if I've never received a royalty check?
faqs.answer: Yes, unleased or non-producing interests can still be purchased, though the offer reflects the current production status.

faqs.question: How do you handle a mineral interest split between several siblings?
faqs.answer: We can purchase each sibling's undivided share individually, or coordinate a single closing if everyone wants to sell at once, whichever fits the family's situation.
